properties.name: Every `--stop-shared` leaves a zombie: the `--shared` client forks `--serve-shared` daemons and never wait()s for them. NINE defunct reflow2-mcp processes accumulated over 27 hours on one machine, the oldest 23h33m
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at main `a000bc7`, found while diagnosing interactive lag the user reported — and it turned out NOT to be the cause, which is the part worth writing down.

═══ THE MECHANISM, READ OFF THE PROCESS TABLE ═══

    pid 3828662  reflow2-mcp --graph-path ./.reflow2/graph --shared     ELAPSED 1-03:26:10
      ├─ 758519   reflow2-mcp ... --serve-shared        S    RSS 299 MB   02:13:54   ← the live daemon
      ├─ 599201   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        02:46:05
      ├─ 478637   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        09:15:59
      ├─ 291284   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        10:04:39
      ├─ 211254   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        11:04:48
      ├─ 121029   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        13:47:45
      ├─ 119935   [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        13:51:29
      └─ 4129702  [reflow2-mcp] <defunct>               Z    RSS 0        23:33:48

    total defunct reflow2-mcp: 9

The `--shared` process is the CLIENT the harness launches and it lives for the whole session (27 hours here). It forks a `--serve-shared` daemon when none is running. `--stop-shared` asks that daemon to exit — and **the parent never `wait()`s**, so the exited child stays in the process table as a zombie. One per restart, and the restarts are not rare: a NEW MCP TOOL is not callable until the server is bounced, so a session that adds tools bounces it repeatedly. This one did so four or five times in a day.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT IT IS NOT, AND THIS IS THE POINT ═══

**IT DID NOT CAUSE THE LAG, AND THE OBVIOUS READING SAYS IT DID.** Nine leaked processes with `reflow2-mcp` in the name looks exactly like a resource leak. Measured: every zombie holds **RSS 0 and 0% CPU** — a zombie is a process-table entry and nothing else. The actual cause was `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=2` on a **4-core** box driving load average to **5.8**; renicing it to +19 dropped that to 4.4 within seconds and it finished green at 1.99.

⇒ Two defects were visible at once and only one was doing harm. Reporting the zombies as the cause would have been a confident, plausible, wrong diagnosis — and the fix would have changed nothing the user could feel.

═══ WHY IT STILL MATTERS ═══

A zombie costs a PID-table entry, not memory. Nine is harmless. But it is unbounded in the length of a session and one-per-bounce, and the thing that forces bounces — a new tool being uncallable until restart — is a normal part of developing reflow2 itself. A long-lived server on a busy machine accumulates them indefinitely.

📌 THE FIX IS ORDINARY: `wait()` on the child after asking it to stop, or double-fork the daemon so `init` reaps it, or set `SIGCHLD` to `SIG_IGN` in the `--shared` client. None of that is architecture.

⚠️ BOUNDS: one machine, one 27-hour session, Linux. The count is what THIS session produced; nothing here says how a fleet or a hosted tier behaves, and no fix has been attempted or verified.
